steps.description: Amend plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: replace `claimed:<machine>` with `zbuild:claimed` in claim_coordinator_claim (remove local our_label and machine logic) and in claim_coordinator_release; add _ccgl_read_holder to extract the holder from the issue's run-status comment, filtering comments by the authenticated GitHub actor (gh api user --jq .login) before scanning for the zbuild-holder field (local-fs backend reads from ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE per-issue file); claim_coordinator_claim returns {"acquired": false, "holder": "<holder>"} on conflict; remove any source of core/claim/claim.sh from plugin.sh (the dependency arrow is claim.sh→registry→plugin.sh, not the reverse)

Update plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/README.md: remove all references to claimed:<machine>; describe the single shared label zbuild:claimed; update ZBUILD_CLAIM_MACHINE_ID row to note it now affects only the holder string in the run-status comment, not the label name
Edit scripts/lib/run-status-render.sh: add <!-- zbuild-holder: CI_URL --> (CI) or <!-- zbuild-holder: run_id=X machine=H --> (local) in rsc_render_header after the run_id marker

Create core/claim/claim.sh: wiring bridge that calls claim-coordinator hooks through the plugin registry; sources core/plugin-registry/registry.sh via $_ZBUILD_ROOT at top (idempotent — registry.sh has a guard; needed because runner.sh sources claim.sh before registry.sh); zbuild_claim_build_holder uses ${HOSTNAME} bash variable (no fork); zbuild_claim_acquire returns 0 immediately without calling discover_plugins or any coordinator hook when issue is empty; zbuild_claim_acquire uses discover_plugins filtered by kind claim-coordinator to find coordinator_dir, stores it in _ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR; calls plugin_hook_call "$coordinator_dir" claim "$issue" with stdout captured to get JSON; on acquired:false sanitizes holder string (strip ANSI codes via sed) and stores in _ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER, returns 1; on backend error (no coordinator found or non-zero hook exit) warns stderr and returns 0 (graceful degradation); on success sets _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED; zbuild_claim_release returns 0 immediately without calling any coordinator hook when _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is unset; zbuild_claim_release MUST unset _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED BEFORE calling plugin_hook_call "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" release "$issue" (makes second call a no-op for DSCLA-13); no direct source of plugin.sh, no _ccgl_* calls, no direct gh calls
Register pipeline.refused.claimed in config/event-schema.json following the pattern of pipeline.refused.issue_locked

Wire core/claim/claim.sh into runner.sh: source at top (already in working copy); call zbuild_claim_build_holder before sidecar spawn; call zbuild_claim_acquire after zbuild_issue_lock_acquire; on refusal emit event + print holder via printf '%s\n' (not error() which uses echo -e) + return 1; call zbuild_claim_release in _runner_abort_trap with declare -F guard, placed AFTER the trap '' INT TERM guard; in both early-failure return paths after zbuild_claim_acquire succeeds but before the EXIT trap is installed, add zbuild_claim_release || true alongside the existing zbuild_run_cap_release || true

Amend docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md: in the ## Enforced by section, extend the §1 bullet to add: §1(a) enforcement claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh [DSCLA-22] (claim hook called after admission lock and before first stage; release hook called in EXIT path); §1(c) enforcement claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh [DSCLA-3] (refused: non-zero exit, no stage dispatched, event emitted) and claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh [DSCLA-9] (refused output names holder); extend the §2 bullet to name [DSCLA-1] for the "shared label is zbuild:claimed (no hostname)" statement, and [DSCLA-2] and [DSCLA-12] for the holder rendering cases

Amend docs/adr/ADR-059-issue-vs-run-keying.md: add an Enforced by entry for the §4 cross-machine exclusion statement — naming [DSCLA-3] (a run is refused when another machine holds zbuild:claimed on the issue)

specs.DSCLA-1:
When an issue-bound run starts and zbuild:claimed is absent, the label is added before the first stage dispatches
  Given: a run is started with an issue number; zbuild:claimed is not on the issue
  When: the run starts
  Then: gh is called to add exactly the label zbuild:claimed to the issue (no hostname component in the label name)
  And: no stage has yet been dispatched
specs.DSCLA-3:
When a run starts on a claimed issue, it refuses with non-zero exit before any stage
  Given: zbuild:claimed is already on the issue
  When: a run is started on that issue
  Then: the run exits non-zero
  And: no stage is dispatched
  And: pipeline.refused.claimed is emitted to the event bus
specs.DSCLA-9:
When a run is refused because zbuild:claimed is on the issue, the run's output names the holder
  Given: zbuild:claimed is on the issue; the existing run-status comment contains a <!-- zbuild-holder: --> field with the holder string
  When: the run exits after finding zbuild:claimed on the issue
  Then: the run's stdout or stderr output contains the holder string from the <!-- zbuild-holder: --> field
specs.DSCLA-18:
When claim_coordinator_claim is called on an issue with no zbuild:claimed label, it adds the label zbuild:claimed via gh issue edit
  Given: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh is loaded; the issue has no zbuild:claimed label
  When: claim_coordinator_claim is called with the issue number
  Then: gh issue edit is called to add the label zbuild:claimed to the issue
  And: the label added has no hostname component
specs.DSCLA-20:
When claim_coordinator_release is called on an issue, it removes the label zbuild:claimed via gh issue edit
  Given: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh is loaded; the issue has the zbuild:claimed label
  When: claim_coordinator_release is called with the issue number
  Then: gh issue edit is called to remove the label zbuild:claimed from the issue
specs.DSCLA-23:
When _ccgl_read_holder reads the holder from the issue's comments, it only reads from comments authored by the authenticated GitHub actor
  Given: the issue has two comments that each contain <!-- zbuild-run-status --> and <!-- zbuild-holder: -->; one was posted by the authenticated actor and one by a different user
  When: _ccgl_read_holder is called with the issue number
  Then: the holder string returned is taken from the authenticated actor's comment, not from the other user's comment
specs.DSCLA-14: README.md in plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/ tells the reader the shared claim label is zbuild:claimed (not claimed:<machine>) and does not reference machine-suffixed labels
specs.DSCLA-2:
When a local run starts with an issue, rsc_render_header embeds the holder in the run-status comment header
  Given: a local run (GITHUB_ACTIONS not true) starts with an issue number; the holder string is run_id=X machine=H
  When: rsc_render_header is called with the run id and holder string
  Then: the rendered header contains <!-- zbuild-holder: run_id=<id> machine=<hostname> -->
specs.DSCLA-12:
When a CI run starts with an issue, the rendered run-status comment header contains the CI run URL as the holder
  Given: a CI run (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true) starts with an issue number
  When: rsc_render_header is called with the run id and the CI holder string
  Then: the rendered header contains <!-- zbuild-holder: <GITHUB_SERVER_URL>/<GITHUB_REPOSITORY>/actions/runs/<GITHUB_RUN_ID> -->
specs.DSCLA-8:
When zbuild_claim_acquire is called with an empty issue argument, it returns 0 without calling the coordinator's claim hook
  Given: core/claim/claim.sh is loaded
  When: zbuild_claim_acquire is called with an empty string as the issue argument
  Then: the function returns 0
  And: the coordinator's claim hook is not called
specs.DSCLA-13:
When a second SIGTERM arrives during the runner's claim release, zbuild:claimed is still removed
  Given: the claim was acquired at run start; the runner has entered _runner_abort_trap and blocked SIGTERM via trap '' TERM
  When: a second SIGTERM arrives while zbuild_claim_release is executing inside _runner_abort_trap
  Then: zbuild:claimed is absent from the issue after the runner exits
specs.DSCLA-15:
The holder string is printed without interpreting escape sequences in the run's refusal output
  Given: the holder string extracted from the GitHub run-status comment contains a backslash sequence such as \n or an ANSI escape code
  When: the run prints the holder on refusal
  Then: the run's stdout or stderr output contains the literal backslash sequence, not its interpreted form
specs.DSCLA-17:
When zbuild_claim_release is called without a prior successful acquire, it returns 0 without calling the coordinator's release hook
  Given: core/claim/claim.sh is loaded; _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is not set
  When: zbuild_claim_release is called
  Then: the coordinator's release hook is not called
specs.DSCLA-19:
When zbuild_claim_acquire is called with an issue number, it delegates to the claim-coordinator plugin's claim hook and contains no direct gh calls
  Given: core/claim/claim.sh is loaded; a claim-coordinator plugin is registered in the discovery tree; that plugin's claim hook returns {"acquired": true} on stdout
  When: zbuild_claim_acquire is called with an issue number
  Then: the claim-coordinator plugin's claim hook function is called with the issue number
  And: gh is not invoked directly within zbuild_claim_acquire
specs.DSCLA-21:
When zbuild_claim_release is called after a prior successful acquire, it delegates to the claim-coordinator plugin's release hook and contains no direct gh calls
  Given: core/claim/claim.sh is loaded; _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is set
  When: zbuild_claim_release is called with the issue number
  Then: the claim-coordinator plugin's release hook function is called with the issue number
  And: gh is not invoked directly within zbuild_claim_release
specs.DSCLA-10:
When the event-schema emitted-coverage check runs, it accepts pipeline.refused.claimed as a registered event
  Given: config/event-schema.json includes an entry for pipeline.refused.claimed
  When: the event-schema emitted-coverage check runs against the codebase
  Then: the check exits without reporting pipeline.refused.claimed as an unregistered event name
specs.DSCLA-5:
On normal pipeline completion, zbuild:claimed is removed from the issue
  Given: the claim was acquired at run start
  When: the pipeline completes normally
  Then: zbuild:claimed is absent from the issue
specs.DSCLA-6:
On pipeline failure, zbuild:claimed is removed from the issue
  Given: the claim was acquired at run start
  When: the pipeline exits due to a stage failure
  Then: zbuild:claimed is absent from the issue
specs.DSCLA-7:
On TERM signal, zbuild:claimed is removed from the issue
  Given: the claim was acquired at run start
  When: the runner process receives SIGTERM
  Then: zbuild:claimed is absent from the issue
specs.DSCLA-16:
When claim acquisition succeeds but runner infrastructure setup fails before the EXIT trap is installed, zbuild:claimed is removed before the runner function returns
  Given: zbuild_claim_acquire succeeds (zbuild:claimed is added to the issue); the subsequent _runner_enter_worktree or zbuild_run_branch_setup call fails before the EXIT trap is installed
  When: the runner returns from that failure path
  Then: zbuild_claim_release is called and zbuild:claimed is absent from the issue after the return
specs.DSCLA-22:
When a stub claim coordinator is registered in the plugin discovery tree and an issue-bound run executes, the stub's claim hook is called before the first stage and its release hook is called on exit
  Given: a stub claim-coordinator plugin is present in the ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT discovery tree; a run starts with an issue number
  When: the run executes and exits normally
  Then: the stub's claim hook is called before the first stage is dispatched
  And: the stub's release hook is called on exit
specs.DSADR-4: ADR-005 tells the reader that the engine calls the claim coordinator's claim hook after the admission lock and before the first stage, and release in the EXIT path
specs.DSADR-5: ADR-005 tells the reader that the shared claim label is zbuild:claimed (no hostname) and that the holder is identified in the run-status comment
specs.DSADR-6: ADR-005 corrects stale content: coordinator selection is not from config/zbuild.yaml, and the engine now has a built-in claim mechanism
specs.DSADR-7: ADR-005 has an ## Enforced by section with the §1 bullet naming a test for each §1 statement: §1(a) claim hook called after admission lock and before first stage — claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh [DSCLA-22]; §1(b) release hook called in the EXIT path — claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh [DSCLA-22]; §1(c) refused run exits non-zero with no stage and event emitted — claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh [DSCLA-3]; §1(c) refused output names holder — claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh [DSCLA-9]; and the §2 bullet naming [DSCLA-1] for the "shared label is zbuild:claimed (no hostname)" statement and [DSCLA-2] and [DSCLA-12] for the holder rendering cases
specs.DSADR-8: ADR-059 §4 tells the reader that cross-machine exclusion is the claim coordinator's job and the admission lock (flock) handles intra-machine serialisation; the amendment's Enforced by entry names DSCLA-3 as the test that enforces the cross-machine exclusion statement
